name: Question 5
problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=x+2y,\,y(0)=1
$$

We wish to approximate the solution using the modified Euler method. Given that the step size is $Δx=\frac{1}{2},$ fill the missing entries in the table below.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} | {{field-3}} |
worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,{y}_{0}=y({x}_{0}),
$$

the predictor equation of the modified Euler method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ{y}_{p}={y}^{′}\cdot Δx.\end{aligned}
$$

The initially predicted new $y$-value is then given by ${y}_{p}=y+Δ{y}_{p}.$

First, we compute the value of ${y}^{′}$ according to the given rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =x+2y \\  & =0+2\cdot 1 \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, we add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |  |  |

Next, we compute $Δ{y}_{p}$ using the predictor equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ{y}_{p} & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

We add this value to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $1$ |  |

Hence, according to the predictor equation, the initially predicted new $y$-value is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p} & =y+Δ{y}_{p} \\  & =1+1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the completed table is as given below.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $1$ | $2$ |

EXPLANATION

For an initial value problem y′=f(x,y),y0=y(x0), the predictor equation of the modified Euler method with step size Δx is given by Δyp=y′⋅Δx. The initially predicted new y-value is then given by yp=y+Δyp.

First, we compute the value of y′ according to the given rule:

y′=x+2y=0+2⋅1=2

So, we add this to our table.

x y y′ Δyp yp
0 1 2

Next, we compute Δyp using the predictor equation:

Δyp=y′⋅Δx=2⋅12=1

We add this value to our table.

x y y′ Δyp yp
0 1 2 1

Hence, according to the predictor equation, the initially predicted new y-value is

yp=y+Δyp=1+1=2.

Therefore, the completed table is as given below.

x y y′ Δyp yp
0 1 2 1 2
